newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bank Bira says 1996 net jumps.
newsitem.headline: Bank Bira says 1996 net jumps.

text.p: Indonesia's Bank Bira posted a net profit of 60 billion rupiah in 1996, compared with 30.34 billion rupiah in 1995, the bank's coporate financial adviser Parven Gandhi told Reuters on Monday.
"The profit is higher than our forecast of $53.8 billion rupiah," he said. "This is the third year that we had to revise up our full year results."
He said that in 1995, the bank revised upwards its net profit by 20 percent and by 10 percent in 1994.
Gandhi said the bank arranged $2.0 billion worth of commercial papers in 1996, against $1.0 billion in 1995. He expected the growth to be around 25 percent this year.
He was upbeat that the commercial paper market in Indonesia was promising and faced little risk so long as the companies arranged were "good ones".
He said rating company, Pefindo, had also given a boost to the market as it was working closely with respected foreign rating agencies.
He said the number of companies issuing commercial papers arranged by Bank Bira totalled 57 in 1996, up from 41 in 1995.
At an economic conference organised by ING Baring Securities Indonesia, he said that over the last three years none of the commercial papers arranged by Bank Bira had defaulted.
Overall, there were only two cases of default over the last three years, he said.
